newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-KLIM SENDS OUT WARNING IN PAN PAC HEATS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-KLIM SENDS OUT WARNING IN PAN PAC HEATS.

text.p: Michael Klim set an Australian and Commonwealth record with the fastest time this year in the men's 100 freestyle heats at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships on Monday.
Olympic champion Penny Heyns of South Africa topped the heats in the women's 100 metres breaststroke against Australia's Samantha Riley.
Klim's record-setting time of 49.52 seconds put him ahead of Ricardo Busquests of Puerto Rico and American Neil Walker going into Monday night's finals.
Kilm won the 200 metres freestyle title on Sunday.
Overall, the United States dominated Monday's session with the top qualifiers in four of the six preliminary events in the morning.
Dolan's asthma attack occured while the Olympic champion swam the men's 400 individual medley.
Dolan finished in four minutes 30.11 seconds, far off his world record of 4:12.30. American Tom Wilkens won in 4:20.47, ahead of Australians Matthew Dunn and Trent Steed.
"At the start of the breaststroke, my chest tightened and I couldn't breathe. I almost drowned in the freestyle," said Dolan, who had a two-second lead going into the last leg of the race.
It was apparent something was wrong and Dolan could be seen gasping for air as he swam the freestyle leg.
Heyns' time of 1:08.65 was slightly better than that of her great Australian rival Riley (1:08.78), who took the bronze in Atlanta.

The championships, which end on Wednesday, have attracted about 300 swimmers from 22 countries and regions, and are one of the last important events on the swimming calendar prior to next January's world championships.
